caption: Asteroid works · Surface anchorage
description: A low processing bridge is pinned into a broken rock ledge. A feed line connects the cutting head, separator and cargo cassette.
prompt: Ultra-wide 16:9 deep-space documentary reconstruction, an uncrewed resource extraction works physically anchored to a large charcoal near-Earth asteroid. Oblique close flyby at industrial inspection distance. The rocky body's curved, broken horizon runs diagonally down across the frame; sunlit coarse breccia, fissures and deep crags fill the bottom and right, black unlit space top left. Concentrate the readable machinery in the middle-right: a long low asymmetric graphite lattice service bridge hugs a ledge, four substantial bolted feet and deeply embedded anchor collars visibly marry it to the uneven rock. A sheltered cutting head disappears into a shadowed cut in the rock; enclosed auger line carries fragments up to a pale ceramic-clad separation vessel, short row of strapped pressure tanks and a docked cargo cassette. Functional pipes, foil wraps, worn stencilless off-white panels, a few ochre fasteners. Make geological scale convincing: facility occupies a fraction of the rugged geological landscape but clearly readable. Realistic optical detail, raking white sunlight, crisp cast shadows with gentle reflected fill, immense quiet. No atmospheric haze, exhaust, planets, text, labels, floating installation, toy-like pedestal, people or explosions. This will be full-bleed behind left-side titles: leave left third quiet and dark, keep mechanism and connected feet within right half and vertical middle of frame.
